static_traits.name: Chen Sikai
static_traits.family_status: Living alone in a large city, with no immediate family nearby
static_traits.social_status: Has a few close friends to talk about personal problems with; because of avoiding games, relationships with fellow-enthusiast friends are affected; friends may not fully understand the emotional significance of games to him
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical disease; no history of similar psychological problems; has not previously received psychotherapy or counseling
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, relatively good logic, high cooperation; dejected tone; often uses cognitive patterns such as catastrophizing, overgeneralization, all-or-nothing thinking, fortune telling, and mental filtering

basic_info.main_problem: After being disappointed by a recently purchased video game, I fell into disappointment and believe I will never find a fun game again.
basic_info.core_demands: Because the decline of interest in games has begun to affect my mood and overall enjoyment of leisure activities, I decided to seek counseling.

core_beliefs: I can no longer find things that make me happy (games can no longer bring pleasure)
Disappointment is inevitable, future attempts will only waste time and energy

special_situations.event: A recently purchased and highly anticipated video game ultimately disappointed (money and time invested, result below expectations)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If a highly anticipated experience ends in disappointment, then similar experiences afterward will be the same; if one game disappoints me, other games will also disappoint me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding playing games, trying to distract attention with other hobbies but difficulty persisting
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Trying again will only lead to disappointment; playing games has become meaningless

special_situations.event: Moments after work when thinking of playing games or trying a new game
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I try again, it will inevitably waste time and money; only a perfect experience is worth investing in
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding or postponing trying new games, reducing contact with game-related content
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This will be another waste; not worth trying

special_situations.event: Social situations of gathering with friends who love games or talking about games
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot enjoy the game, I will ruin the atmosphere or make the relationship awkward; participating will only expose my problems
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids social activities with gaming friends, reducing interaction
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I feel terrible now; going will not be any fun either

special_situations.event: Recalling past positive experiences with games (immersion and a sense of achievement)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Past good experiences were merely chance and are unlikely to happen again in the future; only replicating good experiences of the same level counts as meaningful
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Devaluing positive memories to lower expectations and maintain avoidance
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Those good experiences were just luck; they will not happen again

core_conflict.wish: Longs to gain stable pleasure and relaxation through games, regaining immersion and a sense of achievement
core_conflict.fear: Fears being disappointed again and wasting the investment, worries that losing the main way of relaxing will lead to emptiness and low mood
defense_goal: Controls expectations and emotional fluctuations by avoiding and devaluing positive experiences, maintaining a surface sense of safety

object_relations.self_representation: An alienated person who has lost enjoyment and feels helpless
object_relations.object_representation: Fellow hobbyist friends who do not understand its emotional significance (may continue to be enthusiastic about games)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes that 'not all games will be disappointing' or invites them to try testing the belief in small steps
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Experiences the counselor's suggestions as overly optimistic and possibly underestimating their emotional suffering, thus worrying about being forced to repeat failures
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Use a gentle and steady tone, first empathizing with their disappointment and fear; avoid excessive reasoning, invite them to attend to present bodily and emotional experiences, use open-ended questions and concretizing guidance (such as 'when you think about trying, where in your body feels tightest?'), and gradually receive their hesitation.

manifestations: A sense of 'emptiness' after losing the main leisure method, 'everything seems futile'
Doubt about and sense of hopelessness toward future gaming experiences
outcomes: Avoidance of games and related socializing

manifestations: Avoiding spending time with gaming friends
Believes friends can hardly understand the emotional significance of games to oneself
outcomes: Relationship estrangement and increased sense of loneliness

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact.
manifestations: Discusses in the manner of 'logically I can understand, but emotionally I cannot do it', weakening direct emotional contact
Replacing direct investment in game experience with watching reviews/videos to reduce risk
When talking about disappointment, using rational analysis more than carefully feeling present emotions

positive_force: Having several close friends who can provide emotional support
Past positive experiences of immersion and achievement in games prove the capacity to obtain enjoyment
Able to cope with disappointment in other domains by shifting attention, possessing some self-regulation strategies
negative_force: Negative cognitive patterns such as catastrophizing, overgeneralization, all-or-nothing thinking, and fortune-telling reinforce expectations of disappointment
Avoidance behavior maintains the problem cycle, further weakening interest and socializing
Strong fear of being disappointed again leads to decreased sense of meaning and experience of emptiness
Emotional reasoning makes negative experiences override positive memories and evidence

antecedent: Moments of thinking about or trying to engage with games
The time after work originally meant for relaxation
target_behavior.core_reason: The most recent highly anticipated game experience ended in disappointment, triggering catastrophizing and overgeneralization about future experiences, fearing wasting time and money again
target_behavior.function: Escaping unpleasant emotions and potential feelings of failure, maintaining short-term psychological safety
target_behavior.consequence: Loses the main way of relaxing, low mood and unease increase, and the rhythm of leisure and self-care is disrupted

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding social interaction with gaming friends
antecedent: Friends invite one to play together or talk about games
Social scenes of gathering with fellow enthusiasts
target_behavior.core_reason: Worries that being unable to enjoy it will cause embarrassment or being seen as 'having a problem', and presumes negative outcomes through emotional reasoning
target_behavior.function: Avoids discomfort and potential evaluation in socializing, reducing exposure to triggering cues
target_behavior.consequence: Relationships become distant and loneliness intensifies; use of social support decreases
